children: NielsenIQ (NYSE: NIQ), a global leader in consumer intelligence, today announced new findings from its Agentic Commerce Tracker showing that 51% of U.S. consumers have used at least one AI-powered tool to support their shopping in the past month. The results mark a significant milestone in how consumers discover, evaluate, and purchase products, and offer an early signal of how the data-driven economy is being reshaped by AI.

The findings arrive as brands and retailers face mounting pressure to adapt to a rapidly shifting path to purchase. As AI tools take on a growing role in product discovery and decision-making, product content quality, digital discoverability, and structured product information are becoming as critical to sales performance as traditional merchandising and search visibility.

Adoption spans the full path to purchase, from product discovery through final purchase decisions, rather than a single touchpoint.

“Crossing the 50 percent threshold is a defining moment for the industry,” said Liz Buchanan, President of North America, NIQ. “Just months ago, AI-assisted shopping was viewed as an emerging behavior among early adopters. Today, it is now mainstream. With a majority of consumers now using AI to help them shop, the U.S. has reached a tipping point where AI is shaping how products are discovered, evaluated, and ultimately purchased.”

As adoption accelerates, NIQ is expanding its measurement capabilities to give brands and retailers visibility into how AI tools are reshaping category performance, brand discovery, and purchase conversion—insights that have historically been difficult to isolate from traditional retail and search channels.

“The brands and retailers that succeed in this next era of commerce will be those that optimize not only for consumers, but also for the AI systems helping consumers navigate their choices,” Buchanan added. “The path to purchase is rapidly evolving from search-driven to AI-driven, and that change is happening faster than many organizations realize.”
FAQs
What does NIQ’s latest research show about the role of AI in shopping today?

The newly released research shows that AI is influencing how consumers compare options, evaluate value, and narrow choices during the shopping journey. 51% of U.S. consumers report using at least one AI-powered tool to support shopping in the past month. This marks the first time adoption has crossed the halfway mark.
How is AI changing the consumer decision journey, according to the research?
Rather than replacing shopping, AI is compressing decision-making. Respondents reported using AI to compare options, evaluate value, and narrow choices during the shopping journey.
How can brands and retailers stay informed on NIQ’s agentic commerce research?

NIQ will continue to share updated research findings on an ongoing basis. Data cited in this release comes from NIQ’s proprietary agentic commerce tracker, which is a monthly series being conducted in the United States focused on agentic commerce and adoption among U.S. consumers.
About the NIQ Agentic Commerce Tracker

The NIQ Agentic Commerce Tracker is a monthly study designed to measure consumer adoption of AI-powered shopping tools and understand how artificial intelligence is reshaping the path to purchase. The tracker monitors usage trends, consumer attitudes, and emerging behaviors across the U.S. and Canada markets, to help brands and retailers prepare for the next generation of commerce.
Methodology
NIQ’s findings are based on its ongoing Quick Question research, with a monthly sample of approximately 500 consumers across the United States in 2026.
About NIQ

NielsenIQ (NYSE: NIQ) is a leading consumer intelligence company, delivering the most complete and trusted understanding of consumer buying behavior and revealing new pathways to growth.
